3: Our objectives were to estimate the prevalence of undisclosed discrepancies between prospectively registered study plans and their associated publication. We further aimed to identify the research disciplines where these discrepancies have been observed, whether interventions to reduce discrepancies have been conducted, and gaps in the literature.
4:

40: ```{r setup, include = FALSE}
41: knitr::opts_chunk$set(include = FALSE) # This option stops the code chunks from being output from the knit.
42: ```
43: 
44: ```{r load_packages}
45: library(meta) # For meta-analyses and forest plots.
46: library(irr) # For inter-rater agreement
47: library(knitr) # For kable function.
48: library(kableExtra) # For kable table styling.
49: library(english) # To convert numbers to word equivalents via words(). 
50: library(boot) # For inv.logit() function.
51: library(tidyverse) # For cleaner code.
52: ```
53: ```{r function_metaDisc}
54: # For running meta-analyses on proportions (most of the meta analyses in this review).
55: 
56: metaDisc <- function(df){
57:   # initialize a dataframe to hold all 40 meta-analytic estimates, CIs, PIs, and number of articles analyzed.
58:   estim <- data.frame(matrix(ncol = 7, nrow = length(df)))
59:   colnames(estim) <- c("b", "lower.random", "upper.random", "lower.predict", "upper.predict", "k", "n")
60:   
61:   # assign the colnames from df to the rownames for estim so that the results line up in the next section of code
62:   rownames(estim) <- colnames(df)
63:   
64:   # initialize lists of lists to hold the results of the 40 meta-analyses
65:   metaList<-list()
66:   
67:   # calculate the meta-analytic estimates, CIs, PIs, and number of articles analyzed for outcomes from prospectively registered studies
68:   for (i in grep("discProAny", colnames(df)):grep("discProTime", colnames(df))){
69:     if (sum(!is.na(df[,i] > 0 ))){
70:       # create temporary dataframe with the NAs removed. This is necessary to align the article author and year with the correct article after running each meta-analysis
71:       dfMeta <- df %>% filter(!is.na(df[,i]))
72:       meta <- meta::metaprop(dfMeta[,i], dfMeta$discProDenom,
73:                           # method for conducting the meta-analytic model (a multi-level regression)
74:                           method="GLMM",
75:                           # method to calculate tau
76:                           method.tau="ML",
77:                           # method to calculate the confidence interval for tau^2 (which we don't report)
78:                           method.tau.ci="J", 
79:                           comb.random=TRUE, 
80:                           prediction=TRUE,
81:                           level.predict=0.95,
82:                           # helpful for meta-analyses of few articles (modifies Student's T-distribution)
83:                           hakn=TRUE
84:       )
85:       # create the study labels for the forest plots
86:       meta$studlab <- paste(dfMeta$author, dfMeta$pubYear)
87:       
88:     metaList[[i]] <- meta #store a list of the meta variable for all 40 meta-analyses to make forest plots later
89:     # All meta-analytic estimates, CIs, and PIs, need to have inv.logit() run on them to reverse the logit() function that is used in the metaprop() function. 
90:     estim[i,] <- c(inv.logit(meta$TE.random), 
91:                    inv.logit(meta$lower.random), 
92:                    inv.logit(meta$upper.random),
93:                    inv.logit(meta$lower.predict),
94:                    inv.logit(meta$upper.predict),
95:                    meta$k,
96:                    sum(meta$data[,2]))
97:         }
98:   }
99:   
100:   # same as above for outcomes from studies with unclear timing of registration.
101:   for (i in grep("discAny", colnames(df)):grep("discTime", colnames(df))){
102:     if (sum(!is.na(df[,i] > 0 ))){
103:       
104:       # create temporary dataframe with the NAs removed
105:       dfMeta <- df %>% filter(!is.na(df[,i]))
106:       meta <- meta::metaprop(dfMeta[,i], dfMeta$discDenom,
107:                              method="GLMM", 
108:                              method.tau="ML", 
109:                              method.tau.ci="J", 
110:                              comb.random=TRUE, 
111:                              prediction=TRUE,
112:                              level.predict=0.95,
113:                              hakn=TRUE
114:       )
115:       meta$studlab <- paste(dfMeta$author, dfMeta$pubYear)
116:       
117:       metaList[[i]] <- meta # store a list of the meta variable for all 40 meta-analyses to make forest plots later
118:       estim[i,] <- c(inv.logit(meta$TE.random), 
119:                      inv.logit(meta$lower.random), 
120:                      inv.logit(meta$upper.random),
121:                      inv.logit(meta$lower.predict),
122:                      inv.logit(meta$upper.predict),
123:                      meta$k,
124:                      sum(meta$data[,2]))
125:     }
126:   }
127:       
128: 
129:   # same as above for non-outcome discrepancies for both prospectively and unclear timing of registration articles
130:   # Increment by 2 because we have a denominator for each non-outcome discrepancy in the column after the numerator. This is also the reason this block of code needs to be separate from the outcome discrepancies, which all share a denominator.
131:   for (i in seq(from = grep("discProOtherElig", colnames(df))[1], to = grep("discOtherResults", colnames(df))[1], by = 2)) {
132:     if (sum(!is.na(df[,i] > 0 ))){
133:       # create temporary dataframe with the NAs removed
134:       dfMeta <- df %>% filter(!is.na(df[,i]))
135:       meta <- meta::metaprop(dfMeta[,i], dfMeta[,i+1],
136:                              method="GLMM", 
137:                              method.tau="ML", 
138:                              method.tau.ci="J", 
139:                              comb.random=TRUE, 
140:                              prediction=TRUE,
141:                              level.predict=0.95,
142:                              hakn=TRUE
143:       )
144:       meta$studlab <- paste(dfMeta$author, dfMeta$pubYear)
145:       
146:       metaList[[i]] <- meta # store a list of the meta variable for all 40 meta-analyses to make forest plots later
147:       estim[i,] <- c(inv.logit(meta$TE.random), 
148:                      inv.logit(meta$lower.random), 
149:                      inv.logit(meta$upper.random),
150:                      inv.logit(meta$lower.predict),
151:                      inv.logit(meta$upper.predict),
152:                      meta$k,
153:                      sum(meta$data[,2]))
154:     }
155:   }
156:       
157: 
158:   return(list(estim, metaList))
159: }
160: 
161: ```
162: 
163: ```{r function_metaRR}
164: # For running meta-analyses on Risk Ratios (i.e., likelihood ratios). For the exploratory analyses.
165: 
166: metaRR <- function(Ee, Ne, Ec, Nc, df){
167:   
168:   
169:   meta <- meta::metabin(Ee, Ne, Ec, Nc,
170:                        # Risk ratio analysis will not take the parameters below that I used in the other analyses. Instead, they default to method = "MH" and method.tau = "DL"
171:                        # method="GLMM", 
172:                        # method.tau="ML", 
173:                        # method.tau.ci="J", 
174:                         comb.random=TRUE, 
175:                         prediction=TRUE,
176:                         level.predict=0.95,
177:                         hakn=TRUE,
178:                         sm = "RR"
179:   )
180:   
181:     meta$studlab <- paste(df$author, df$pubYear)
182:     
183:     CI <- paste0(round(exp(meta$lower.random),2), "-", round(exp(meta$upper.random),2))  
184:     
185:     #sprintf() is necessary to keep trailing zeros on a PI that = 1.00
186:     PI <- paste0(round(exp(meta$lower.predict),2), "-", sprintf("%.2f", round(exp(meta$upper.predict),3)))
187:                
188:                  
189:   return(list(meta, CI, PI))
190: }
191: ```
192: 
193: ```{r function_makeCI}
194: # To format the confidence intervals in the tables.
195: makeCI <- function(data){
196: 
197:   data <- round(data, 2)
198:   CI <- paste0(data$lower.random*100, "-", data$upper.random*100, "%")
199:   return(CI)
200:   
201:   }
202: ```
203: 
204: ```{r function_makePI}
205: # To format the prediction intervals in the tables.
206: makePI <- function(data){
207:   
208:   data[,1:5] <- data[,1:5]*100
209:   
210:   for (i in 1:nrow(data)){
211:     data[i,4] <- ifelse(data[i,4] < 0.5, signif(data[i,4],1), round(data[i,4],0))
212:     data[i,5] <- ifelse(data[i,5] > 99.5, signif(data[i,5] - 100, 1) + 100, round(data[i,5],0))
213:   }
214:   
215:   PI <- paste0(data$lower.predict, "-", data$upper.predict, "%")
216:   return(PI)
217:   
218:   }
219: ```
220: 
221: 
222: ```{r clean_screening_data}
223: # Import the screening data. Calculate the number of articles in each category. Calculate inter-rater reliability
224: screen <- read.csv("/data/preregSR_dataScreen.csv", header = TRUE)
225: 
226: # Calculate Cohen's kappa for whether articles were marked (1) relevant to systematic or not, and (2) relevant to the scoping review or not. I am doing this as two kappa values for binary variables.
227: screen <- screen %>%  mutate(RCsr = ifelse((RC == "BOTH" | RC == "SR"), 1, 0))
